sources.name: Abel
sources.line: A perfume shop. The range, the scent types, a quiz, a journal.
sources.take: A catalogue. One product at a time.

sources.name: Igloo
sources.line: An onchain community. The public HTML is a shell, so the lesson is the mission they publish, not a layout.
sources.take: A product with one job. Do not invent a homepage they did not ship.

sources.name: Don't Board Me
sources.line: In-home pet care. A loud line, then the services, then book.
sources.take: A service with a next step. The headline can shout. The booking stays plain.

sources.name: Noomo
sources.line: A Los Angeles studio. 3D stories and sites that stop a scroll.
sources.take: One scroll, one story. Motion carries the page.

sources.name: Synchronized
sources.line: A digital studio. The word archive repeats until the work is the page.
sources.take: Lead with the work. Say the name until it holds.

sources.name: Mendo
sources.line: A bookshop in Amsterdam. Books as objects, and a journal beside the shop.
sources.take: Paper, type, and the object. The shop stays quiet.

sources.name: Nixon
sources.line: Watches. The page could not be read from here, so no screen claims it yet.
sources.take: Open the site before a screen borrows from it.

sources.name: Dragone
sources.line: Live shows. A dark front, then the shows, the news, and a way to partner.
sources.take: A show with a way in. Spectacle, then the ask.

sources.name: Nothin'
sources.line: A Paris studio. Ideas, not a pile of content. One line does the work.
sources.take: A short sentence, large. The rest of the page waits.

sources.name: Stripe
sources.line: A payments company. One bright ribbon, a light headline, and the product shown working in every card.
sources.take: Let one big moving thing carry the colour. Keep the words light and the cards real.

sources.name: UseArticle
sources.line: A tool that writes and posts articles on a schedule. The page shows the product running, not a picture of it.
sources.take: Let the visitor press the controls and watch the card change. Thick black edges and hard shadows keep it friendly.

sources.name: Linear
sources.line: A tool for building software. A dark page where the real app is the picture.
sources.take: Show the product doing the work. Fade it at the edges and keep one colour for what matters.

sources.name: Tailwind CSS docs
sources.line: The install page for a CSS framework. Numbered steps, each with its own small code box.
sources.take: Put each instruction next to its code. Draw the grid with thin lines and let the empty sides carry a faint hatch.

sources.name: Wickret
sources.line: A concept bank app page by a studio. One huge headline, toys floating around it, then a phone.
sources.take: Let the big words move. Letters can break apart and come back as new words.

sources.name: Lama Lama
sources.line: An Amsterdam agency. A dark page with a dot screen hero and a small bar that talks back.
sources.take: A tiny nav bar can carry the voice. Change its one line for each section.

sources.name: MindMarket
sources.line: A research agency. Big friendly type on bright green, cartoon people, white cards along a winding path.
sources.take: One path ties the page together. Cards sit beside it, and the numbers pile up as you scroll.

sources.name: The F-List
sources.line: A watchdog report on ad agencies. Black and yellow, tall narrow type, lines hidden under black bars.
sources.take: Make the reveal the message. Bars lift off the text, and badges explain the list.

sources.name: Bermawy
sources.line: A personal site typed on graph paper. A torn photo, clipped cards, a notebook of articles. A toy console plays the talks.
sources.take: Let one toy be the real control. Keep the rest plain and on paper.

sources.name: Haunted Boulder City
sources.line: A ghost walking tour. Fog, night photos and huge narrow type. The story slides sideways as you scroll.
sources.take: Pin the screen and let scroll turn the pages. Only the line you are on gets to shout.

sources.name: GMX Digital
sources.line: A film studio for buildings that are not built yet. Dark, slow, and it plays like a film.
sources.take: Keep the headline still and let the scenes change behind it. A thin line counts down each one.

sources.name: Sibal Design
sources.line: One designer, shown like a ship screen. You press Enter, it loads, then the work opens in frames.
sources.take: Make the entrance a choice and keep it short. Then let each project show its steps, one at a time.

sources.name: MWDT
sources.line: A machine shop. A dark hero card, a steel part, and a button to ask for a quote.
sources.take: Let the product break out of the box. One light line, one heavy line, one button.

sources.name: Moremedia
sources.line: An agency in Austria. Big tight type, real work, and services you open one at a time.
sources.take: Set the services as tall labels. Open one, and keep the rest as type.

sources.name: Susan Acharya
sources.line: A product lead's portfolio. A night valley drawn by hand. Small people play in it while you read.
sources.take: Draw one scene and let it move a little. The words stay calm on top.

sources.name: 60fps
sources.line: A big library of short clips. Small moments from phone apps, tagged by gesture, pattern and effect.
sources.take: Show one small moment at a time, and let the tags do the sorting.

sources.name: Icon Museum
sources.line: A gallery of app icons. Each one sits on a glass shelf. Click one to see it big with its colours.
sources.take: Let the icons be the only colour. Give each one a shelf, a lift on hover, and a quiet label.

families.name: Quiet
families.mood: Hairlines, 6px corners, one solid button. The safe default for products that have to last.
rules: Radius 6px on controls, 8px on cards. Never more.
One solid primary. Secondary is outline, same height (40px web / 44px phone).
Hairline borders at 1px. No drop shadows on tables.
Focus ring 2px accent, 3px offset.

families.name: Soft
families.mood: Tonal fills, 14px corners, pills. Friendly without becoming a toy.
rules: Radius 14px on cards, 999px on chips and the primary button.
Primary is a soft accent wash, not a hard fill, unless contrast needs it.
Plenty of air: 24px gaps, 20px card pad.
Phone targets 44px. No hairlines thinner than 1px.

families.name: Sharp
families.mood: Zero radius, visible grid, type that does the work. Swiss without the poster shout.
rules: Radius 0 everywhere. If you round a button you have left the family.
1px ink rules. No shadows. Alignment is the decoration.
Primary can be a solid ink block; hover inverts.
Uppercase 11px labels, 0.12em tracking, on data and nav.

families.name: Editorial
families.mood: Paper, measure, a serif that holds a room. Buttons stay quiet so the type can speak.
rules: Measure 58–66ch on reading. Headlines can break the grid.
Buttons are outlined, 40px, no fill until hover.
Paper grain or warm off-white is allowed; stock photos are not.
Italic is a voice, used once per viewport.

families.name: Glass
families.mood: Translucent bars, 16px corners, things that float. Native feel on the web.
rules: Bars use backdrop-filter: blur(16px) at ~72% opacity. Always give a solid fallback.
Radius 16px on sheets, 999px on tab pills.
Phone chrome: 44px tab bar, home indicator clearance 10px.
Do not glass a whole page. One floating layer is enough.

families.name: Industrial
families.mood: Utility first. Tight type, 2px corners, labels that read like a yard sheet.
rules: Radius 2px. Dense padding (12px). Tables are first-class.
Primary is a committed fill (accent or ink). 36px on web, 44px on phone.
Mono for numbers. Tabular nums. No ornament.
Status colour is reserved for live state, never decoration.

collections.title: First impressions
collections.blurb: Landing pages, onboarding, empty states and the 404. The screens people meet before they trust you.

collections.title: A website, in parts
collections.blurb: Heroes, navs, features, pricing, proof, contact and the sign-off. Assemble a marketing site from pieces that already agree with each other.

collections.title: Sites that show the work
collections.blurb: Personal and studio portfolios: the index, the case study, the photographer’s rail, the architect’s list. Steal a structure, not a personality.

collections.title: Landing pages with a point of view
collections.blurb: Full first pages for fashion, wellness, fintech, a dev tool and an agency. Each one is a complete argument, not a template.

collections.title: Proof, and the close
collections.blurb: Testimonials, logos, FAQs, stats and the last ask. The blocks that turn a visitor into a customer without raising their voice.

collections.title: Navigation, sorted
collections.blurb: Sidebars, rails, tab bars, drawers and palettes. Every way to get around a product, from a 64px icon rail to a floating glass capsule.

collections.title: Loading states that earn the wait
collections.blurb: Skeletons that match their content, loaders with three elements, buttons that carry their own progress. Nothing spins for the sake of spinning.

collections.title: Sheets, dialogs and things on top
collections.blurb: Bottom sheets with detents, dialogs with real focus traps, toasts that stack, panels that anchor. Layering done with restraint.

collections.title: Forms people finish
collections.blurb: Steppers, inline validation, one-page checkout, sign-in that respects the keyboard. The boring parts, made unboring by getting the details right.

collections.title: The control set
collections.blurb: The field, the button, the badge, the alert, the path, and the pages of a list. One control language, before any screen invents a second.

collections.title: Native feel, web materials
collections.blurb: iOS 26 glass, Material 3 Expressive shapes, and the PWA moments in between: install, offline, update.

collections.title: Dashboards and dense data
collections.blurb: Tables you can live in, KPI rows, boards, bento grids and counters that roll. Density without noise.

collections.title: Motion with a reason
collections.blurb: Transitions that explain where things went. Every duration and curve here is doing a job: continuity, hierarchy, or feedback.

collections.title: Typography does the work
collections.blurb: Pieces where the type is the design: editorial heroes, kinetic marquees, reading pages with a proper measure, spreads that behave like print.

collections.title: Whole design languages
collections.blurb: Not a component, a dialect. Each of these is a complete visual grammar you can hand to an agent as the style guide for a product.

collections.title: Cursor and hover play
collections.blurb: Pieces that answer the pointer: magnetic buttons, image trails, letters that get heavier as you approach, cards that tilt and flip.

collections.title: Scroll as the timeline
collections.blurb: Motion tied to scroll position, not the clock: stacking cards, clip reveals, sticky stories, collapsing titles, reading progress.

collections.title: Widgets and faces
collections.blurb: Clocks, rings, timers and live tiles. The small faces of a bigger app, for home screens, watches and dashboards.

collections.title: Social cards
collections.blurb: Posts, profiles, repos and chat in the shapes people already know, with invented brands.

collections.title: Paper and objects
collections.blurb: Tickets, postcards, polaroids, albums and stamps. Real things people recognise, made in CSS.

collections.title: Backgrounds and buttons
collections.blurb: Surfaces to set a page on and buttons worth pressing: gradients, patterns, keycaps, sheens and holds.

easings.name: Lounge standard
easings.feel: Decisive, a little heavy at the start, lands clean.
easings.use: Default for UI moves: width, opacity, colour, small translates.

easings.name: Expo out
easings.feel: Fast start, long settle. The “it arrived” curve.
easings.use: Hero reveals, shared-element expands, sheets rising.

easings.name: iOS sheet
easings.feel: Apple’s sheet: almost linear, then a soft stop.
easings.use: Bottom sheets, drawers, large vertical translates.

easings.name: Enter
easings.feel: Same as expo out; named so agents pick it for incoming.
easings.use: Anything that appears: toasts, menus, tooltips.

easings.name: Exit
easings.feel: Leaves quickly. Don’t linger on things going away.
easings.use: Dismissals under 180ms. Pair with enter, never the reverse.

easings.name: Emphasized
easings.feel: Material 3 Expressive. Slow, then a committed finish.
easings.use: Container transforms, FAB morphs, large layout changes.

easings.name: Emphasized decelerate
easings.use: Elements entering a scene in Material language.

easings.name: Emphasized accelerate
easings.feel: Outgoing M3 motion. Leaves with intent.

easings.name: Soft spring (approx)
easings.feel: A polite overshoot. One bounce, then still.
easings.use: Likes, checkboxes, small toggles. Never on layout width.

easings.name: Snappy spring (approx)
easings.feel: Playful overshoot. Use once per screen.

easings.name: Linear
easings.feel: No personality. Correct for loops and progress.

easings.name: In–out cubic
easings.feel: Symmetric. Good when the move will reverse.
easings.use: Theme toggles, accordion height, play/pause morphs.

recipes.name: Fade and rise
recipes.note: The Lounge .reveal. Cap stagger at 8 items.

recipes.name: Underline grow
recipes.note: Use a ::after, not text-decoration, so you can ease it.

recipes.name: Sidebar rail
recipes.note: Fade labels out *before* the width finishes so they never wrap.

recipes.name: Sheet up
recipes.note: Dim the scrim on a 240ms linear fade, not the sheet curve.

recipes.name: Dialog in
recipes.note: Focus the first field after the transitionend, not immediately.

recipes.name: Toast enter
recipes.note: Older toasts shift up 8px on the layout curve, not the enter curve.

recipes.name: Tab ink bar
recipes.note: Measure getBoundingClientRect; don’t animate with magic numbers.

recipes.name: Count up
recipes.note: tabular-nums. Never more than four counters on one frame.

recipes.name: SVG stroke draw
recipes.note: Set dasharray to the measured length. Replay resets to length then plays.

recipes.name: Marquee
recipes.note: Duplicate the row so the loop is seamless. Pause on hover.

recipes.name: Like pop
recipes.note: Optimistic: flip state first, then animate.

recipes.name: Page curtain
recipes.note: Hold the outgoing page until the curtain covers, then swap.

recipes.name: Shared expand
recipes.note: One element travels. Don’t fade a new one in on top.

recipes.name: Skeleton to content
recipes.note: Crossfade, don’t pop. Skeleton geometry should match the content.

recipes.name: Magnetic pull
recipes.note: Reset on leave. Never more than 8px of travel.

recipes.name: Theme circle wipe
recipes.note: This is how the Lounge day/night toggle works.
